categories.name: Direct Payment
categories.description: Cases where the fine is created and promptly paid with little or no intermediate notification or administrative overhead.
categories.rationale: High frequency of short traces ending in Payment directly after Create Fine or Send Fine.

categories.name: Standard Fine Collection
categories.description: Standard administrative path involving fine creation, sending, notifications, and penalties, ultimately ending in credit collection due to non-payment.
categories.rationale: Represents the most common heavy-weight lifecycle leading to non-payment and debt collection.

categories.name: Delayed Payment with Penalties
categories.description: Cases that undergo standard notifications and penalty additions before eventually being settled via one or more payments over a longer duration.
categories.rationale: Captures a high frequency of cases where penalties are added and payments occur significantly later than direct payment variants.

categories.name: Prefecture Appeal Path
categories.description: Cases involving formal appeals submitted to the prefecture, sometimes resulting in prefecture review outcomes, additional notifications, and varied final resolutions.
categories.rationale: Identifiable by the insertion of prefecture appeal dates and subsequent prefecture-related activities.

categories.name: Rework-Heavy Payment
categories.description: Extreme or long traces characterized by repeated payment transactions spread out over extended durations.
categories.rationale: Distinct pattern of exceptionally long traces consisting almost entirely of repeated payment steps.
